title: DeepSeek Infra 5.0 Native Rust/Go Runtime Readiness Assessment
assessment_scope: Repository snapshot only; this file is not release evidence.

blockers.detail: Native chat, MCP and A2A routes have local implementations, but the default production listener is still Python. Some modes and public /api paths fail closed; complete behavioral parity, authenticated control proxy and production edge authority remain unqualified.

The cutover state machine is real: schema v8 persists a control-authority-v1 head with an append-only checkpoint journal and append-only cutover authorizations, ClaimControlAuthority is the only path that may advance it, and TransitionCutover promotes a domain only when the deployment opts in (DEEPSEEKD_CONTROL_AUTHORITY, which config refuses without an internal API bearer), the presented checkpoint is the live authority tip, and the revision/epoch/fencing CAS matches. De-promotion needs no authority, so ownership is always recoverable. Every /internal/* control request now requires a loopback bearer (>=32 characters, constant-time, 401 INTERNAL_API_UNAUTHORIZED otherwise, and no control plane at all when unconfigured). Production authority of the worker execution plane is likewise durable: a coordinator that claims it must be backed by the action domain's cutover record. Production mutation application is implemented through the approved control-mutation-request-v2 apply-mutation operation (compat v32, 34 frozen cases replayed by the Python oracle, Go and Rust) with schema v9 admitting an APPLIED result atomically with the record write; cross-language fail-opens (float record bodies, found in all three, and Go's shared secret-key exemption) were found and closed, so every implementation is now at least as strict as the oracle. The authority claim, live-head read, cutover transition and signed v2 apply now have loopback-bearer HTTP routes with isolated local success/refusal tests; cross-domain operation-ID reuse is refused. What still blocks Go production ownership: no production domain has an externally signed per-domain promotion artifact or export/import and rollback evidence, and the ownership contract has not been revised.

The optional worker S3 path now journals placement/condition and requires conditional byte verification, but operation-specific signed admission, provider ownership and full process-kill/takeover recovery remain unqualified. A missing object or mismatched metadata cannot settle an uncertain in-flight write as unapplied; local library results are not release proof. Production authority of the worker execution plane is now durable rather than caller-asserted: the coordinator's four execution/recovery entry points require the action domain's cutover record to say Go owns it, so a self-asserted flag and a larger epoch are both refused with CUTOVER_NOT_AUTHORIZED before any durable write. Still unqualified: operation-specific signed admission to the worker, renewable live authority across a real lease loss, provider-backed kill/takeover evidence, and outcome/risk verification.
Native Three-MinIO, two-Fleet/four-MinIO, and SIGKILL/takeover workload evidence has not been produced.
No exact-head CI and Evidence Assembly artifacts qualify this native runtime snapshot.
Zero-Python and unique-writer invariants have targets and executable gates, but require live workload-measured artifacts.
